# data/interim — generated by `anti-uav convert`, never edited by hand

Each `<dataset>/<variant>/` directory here is written by exactly one command:

```powershell
anti-uav convert --dataset dvb        # writes data/interim/dvb/full/
anti-uav convert --dataset mavvid     # writes data/interim/mavvid/full/
anti-uav convert --dataset antiuav --variant 300   # writes data/interim/antiuav/300/
anti-uav convert --dataset mmuav --variant subset  # writes data/interim/mmuav/subset/
```

The layout is identical in every one of them:

```
<dataset>/<variant>/
  index.jsonl          one FrameRecord per line - the frame index
  convert_report.json  what happened, including every warning
  frames/<sequence>/rgb/<stem>.jpg
  labels/<sequence>/rgb/<stem>.txt
```

## Why the sequence level matters

`<sequence>` is the unit that makes splitting honest. Adjacent frames of a video
are near-identical, so a frame-level train/val split leaks and inflates mAP by
double digits. Grouping frames under a sequence directory is what lets
`anti-uav splits` keep a whole sequence on one side of the boundary.

`convert` normalises every publisher's idiosyncratic layout into this shape, and
the grouping pattern that recognises a sequence is declared per dataset in
`configs/datasets/registry.yaml` under `group.pattern`. It matches the
**normalised** path on purpose — a regex over the publisher's original filenames
would silently change meaning if a folder were renamed upstream.

## index.jsonl

One JSON object per frame. It is the contract between `convert` and everything
downstream (`stats`, `splits`, `build`, `sanity`, `dedup`), and it is written
atomically via a `.tmp` file, so an interrupted convert does not leave a
half-written index that later stages would read as complete.

`anti-uav splits` adds a `split` field to every record. **That is why the order
is convert -> splits -> build -> sanity and not interchangeable:** `build` reads
each record's `split` field, so building before splitting produces an empty
train set and a `sanity` failure.

## convert_report.json

Read this when a number looks wrong. It records per-dataset frame counts, the
label histogram actually observed, every unknown label seen, and every skipped
file. `convert` stops on an unreadable source rather than silently skipping
frames — if this file lists warnings, they are the reason your frame count is
lower than the publisher's figure.

## Cleaning up

These directories are reproducible from `data/raw/`, so they are safe to delete —
but they are also expensive to rebuild (video decode plus focus scoring). Before
deleting, check whether `data/processed/<combo>/build_report.json` already refers
to them.
